hello.note: Reply: ওয়ালাইকুম আসসালাম (walaikum assalam). Hindus and West Bengal use নমস্কার (nomoshkar).

goodbye.note: When you leave: আসি (ashi), 'I'll be off'. In Bangladesh also আল্লাহ হাফেজ (allah hafez).

please.note: Used sparingly; politeness mostly comes from the verb ending, e.g. বসুন (boshun), 'please sit'.

thank_you.note: Said less than in English; with friends and family it can even sound distant.

youre_welcome.note: Literally 'it's no matter'. Bengali has no set reply to thanks; this is the natural one.

yes.note: A nasal 'hæ' sound. Politer, especially in Bangladesh: জি (ji).

no.note: Politer, especially in Bangladesh: জি না (ji na).

sorry.note: English সরি (sori) is just as common day to day. For a bigger apology: মাফ করবেন (maf korben).

excuse_me.note: Literally 'are you listening?'. People often add ভাই (bhai) to a man, আপা/দিদি (apa/didi) to a woman.

good_morning.note: Rather formal. Day to day people use the normal greeting or English গুড মর্নিং (gud morning).

how_are_you.note: To a friend: কেমন আছ? (kemon achho?)

im_fine.note: Often shortened to ভালো, আপনি? (bhalo, apni?), 'fine, and you?'

my_name_is.note: No word for 'is' is needed here.

nice_to_meet_you.text: আপনার সাথে পরিচিত হয়ে ভালো লাগল
nice_to_meet_you.roman: apnar shathe porichito hoye bhalo laglo
nice_to_meet_you.note: In West Bengal সঙ্গে (shonge) is more usual than সাথে (shathe).

where_from.note: Between Bengalis: আপনার বাড়ি কোথায়? (apnar bari kothay?), asking about their home town.

speak_english.note: কি (ki) here just marks a yes/no question.

dont_understand.note: Shorter: বুঝলাম না (bujhlam na), 'I didn't get that'.

speak_slowly.note: Softer: একটু ধীরে বলবেন? (ektu dhire bolben?), 'would you speak a bit slowly?'

what.note: Spelled কী for 'what'; কি (same sound) is the yes/no question marker.

when.note: For which day or date: কবে? (kobe?)

who.note: For more than one person: কারা? (kara?)

how_much.note: At a market, just এটা কত? (eta koto?)

where_bathroom.note: Literally 'can you tell me where the bathroom is?'. টয়লেট (toylet) is also common.

what_time.note: In Bangladesh often কয়টা বাজে? (koyta baje?)

one.note: Digit: ১. When counting things add -টা: একটা (ekta).

two.note: Digit: ২. With things: দুটো (duto), in Bangladesh দুইটা (duita).

water.note: In West Bengal and among Hindus: জল (jol).

tea.note: Usually milky and sweet. Black tea: রং চা (rong cha) in Bangladesh, লিকার চা (likar cha) in West Bengal.

bread.note: Means flatbread (chapati). Sliced loaf bread is পাউরুটি (pauruti).

im_hungry.note: In Bangladesh also: আমার ক্ষুধা লেগেছে (amar khudha legechhe).

menu_please.note: The polite 'will you…?' ending (-ben) does the job of 'please'.

delicious.note: Everyday: খুব মজা হয়েছে! (khub moja hoyechhe!) in Bangladesh, দারুণ খেতে! (darun khete!) in West Bengal.

no_meat.note: Fish doesn't count as meat in Bengal; add মাছও খাই না (machho khai na) if you avoid it too.

enjoy_meal.note: No set phrase exists; hosts say this, 'eat your fill'. Muslims say বিসমিল্লাহ (bismillah) before eating.

left.note: Literally 'to the left side'. In Bangladesh often বাম দিকে (bam dike).

straight_ahead.note: In directions often just সোজা যান (shoja jan), 'go straight'.

stop_here.note: Also natural: এখানে নামিয়ে দিন (ekhane namiye din), 'drop me here'.

airport.note: In speech, এয়ারপোর্ট (eyarport) is just as common.

hotel.note: হোটেল can also mean a cheap eatery; for a place to stay say আবাসিক হোটেল (abashik hotel).

want_to_go.note: To a rickshaw or taxi driver: … যাবেন? (… jaben?), 'will you go to …?'

too_expensive.note: To bargain: একটু কম করুন (ektu kom korun), 'bring it down a little'.

id_like_this.note: Or simply এটা দিন (eta din), 'give me this'.

cash.note: In shops people often just say ক্যাশ (kyash).

big.note: ড় is a quick flapped r with the tongue curled back.

tomorrow.note: In speech just কাল (kal), which also means yesterday; the verb tense tells them apart.

yesterday.note: In speech just কাল (kal), same as 'tomorrow'; the past-tense verb makes it clear.

good_evening.note: Formal; in daily life the normal greeting is used at any hour.

good_night.note: Formal; with friends English গুড নাইট (gud nait) is more usual.

wait_moment.note: Literally 'stand a little'. Also: এক মিনিট (ek minit); formal: একটু অপেক্ষা করুন (ektu opekkha korun).

help.note: Literally 'save (me)!'. Also: কেউ সাহায্য করুন! (keu shahajjo korun!), 'someone help!'

call_police.note: Emergency number: 999 in Bangladesh, 112 in India.

pharmacy.note: Signs usually say ফার্মেসি (farmesi), a word everyone uses.

allergic.note: Attach -তে or -এ to the allergen: চিংড়িতে (chingrite) 'to shrimp', বাদামে (badame) 'to nuts'.

be_careful.note: As a parting 'take care': সাবধানে থাকবেন (shabdhane thakben).

i_like_it.note: For something you just tried: ভালো লেগেছে (bhalo legechhe). Also: এটা আমার পছন্দ (eta amar pochhondo).

im_tired.note: Everyday: আমার খুব ক্লান্ত লাগছে (amar khub klanto lagchhe), 'I feel really tired'.

welcome.note: The warm spoken welcome, 'come in, come in!'. On signs and in speeches: স্বাগতম (shagotom).
